title: tpm20: fix dissector to reassemble fragmented TPM packets

notes.body: You have declared 'bool' but used a mixture of TRUE/FALSE and true/false.  Please use gboolean and TRUE/FALSE.

https://www.iana.org/assignments/service-names-port-numbers/service-names-port-numbers.txt lists "rdlap" for tcp port 2321 and "ofsd" for tcp port 2322, though there doesn't appear to be dissectors for either.  I do realise that you didn't change this part!

Note that if the preference value is changed from the original TCP_TPM_PORTS, check these hardcoded port numbers will no longer be correct.

I don't know of a way to check which of the src/dst ports matched the preference?  Of if you can infer the direction from the packet contents?  Or maybe if the first data frame in a given conversation tells you, could could maybe store which port is which in the conversation info?

Would it instead be possible to look for a value in commands[] and responses[] to infer whether its a request or response? e.g. call try_val_to_str() and check for non-NULL return value?
The pipeline failure suggests you need to check some option in the MR - I don't recognise the error though...

there is the small warning 
`Unused href entry: epan/dissectors/packet-tpm20.c: hf_tpm20_platform_resp_size`

but the major issue coming from using your master branch to this PR (and it is no supported...)

commits_data.title: tpm20: make dissector run over fragmented packets correctly
commits_data.message:
tpm20: make dissector run over fragmented packets correctly

The current tpm20 dissector is assuming a specific fragmentation of
packets (that the command header will be in a 9 byte fragment followed
by the rest of the command in the next fragment, for instance) which
isn't seen in any traces I've taken.  Fix dissection by using the
correct tcp_dissect_pdus() abstraction.

Doing this fix also means we can't distinguish based on fragment size,
so distinguish based on command instead.  Since the command/response
protocol is single threaded, all state can be kept in a single entity
instead of using the wmem btree.

Signed-off-by: James Bottomley <James.Bottomley@HansenPartnership.com>

commits_data.title: tpm20: Make dissected handles a range
commits_data.message:
tpm20: Make dissected handles a range

In TPM2.0 handles are signified by the most significant octet (MSO)
make the print of handles display every handle type (by MSO) using a
range print insted of the specific name of only MSO type 0x40 handles.

Signed-off-by: James Bottomley <James.Bottomley@HansenPartnership.com>
